summary: CookCLI is a command-line utility designed to handle meal planning and shopping list generation using Cooklang recipe files. Written in Rust under an MIT licence, it integrates into UNIX-style scripting workflows and includes an embedded web server for local access.
goodFor: It suits technical users who prefer managing recipes in plain text and automating kitchen logistics via the command line or shell scripts.
watchOut: The command-line interface and text-file format mean there is a steep learning curve compared to traditional graphical recipe managers.
deployNotes: As a compiled Rust binary with an integrated web server, it typically runs as a standalone service behind a reverse proxy for TLS termination, with persistent storage required for your recipe files.
